title: Mixing after unequal filters creates nonzero loop phases in two reversible adult worm circuit models
abstract: We tested a triangle phase test under cross-cell measurement mixing. Two partial adult worm electrical maps supplied reciprocal passive models with equal independent noise. Both latent voltage processes were reversible. We applied unequal scalar low-pass filters, then nonnegative channel mixtures. At frequency one and a 5 percent mixture coefficient, median mean absolute loop sines were 0.00844 and 0.01206 over 50 assumed observation patterns. The median shares passing an earlier 1 percent spectrum-error certificate were 8.33 and 12.50 percent among fixed eligible triangles. This certificate assumes diagonal filters, so it cannot establish latent irreversibility under mixing. Common filters with the same mixtures gave real spectra. An exact three-cell example had a nonzero first derivative of the imaginary triangle product at zero mixture. Thus no positive universal mixture bound preserves an exactly zero loop phase. Direct inverse, Lyapunov and symbolic checks passed. These are population-model results, not measured activity or finite-record error rates. Partial anatomy, assumed filters, random mixing without spatial constraints, and no optical calibration limit transfer. Code, scalar results, hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Mixing after unequal filters creates loop phases in reversible models. Lines show medians over 50 assumed observation patterns. Shading shows 5th to 95th percentiles. The certificate assumes diagonal filters, which mixing violates. These are model scores, not experimental rejection rates.

citations.reason: Prior diagonal-filter loop test and error certificate; we test cross-cell mixing with new code.
Prior frequency-averaging failure; our spectra are at single exact frequencies.
Prior reciprocal model convention and partial map limitations.
